workflow: A global allocation-tracking subsystem records non-owning pointers to metadata strings created inside an isolated execution context.
The context is destroyed and releases those strings while the tracker still retains their pointers.
Later allocation processing or tracker cleanup compares, dereferences, or releases the retained pointers as though they were still valid.
The access reaches freed memory and terminates the process with a use-after-free failure.
summary: Retained metadata pointers outlive isolated-context teardown
